title: Chapter 93: Twenty-four Names
html:
Regardless of what Fan Yu’s aunt had done in the past, at least at that moment, she was putting Fan Yu first.

“I will try my best to watch out for the boy,” Chen Ge promised without hesitation. In this whole incident, Fan Yu was the most innocent.

“You don’t need to worry so much.” The officer behind the desk joined them. “We’ve already contacted child services. If you truly repent, you may still have a chance to see the boy in the future.”

“My child?” Fan Yu’s aunt looked at that officer, and her blank expression slowly shifted. Her lips fell open as she stared at a spot above the officer’s shoulder, and for some reason, she smiled. “Okay, I will tell you everything I know.”

The formal interrogation began. No longer needed, Chen Ge asked to leave. Outside the station, he hailed a taxi to Fan Yu’s home.

The case might appear resolved, but one enormous question remained—one only Chen Ge knew to ask and only Fan Yu could answer.

The sun was rising, yet its light could not penetrate the maze of narrow alleys. After leaving the taxi, Chen Ge followed his memory deeper inside.

At last, he found the apartment Fan Yu’s aunt had rented. He knocked several times on the second-floor door. A lock shifted inside, and the door opened a crack. Chen Ge pushed it wider, but no one stood behind it. He lingered on the threshold. Even with sunlight on his back, he felt no warmth.

“Fan Yu?” The room grew colder as Chen Ge entered. The living room and kitchen were empty. He approached the bedroom and pressed the door. Like the first, it was unlocked and swung open easily.

Heavy curtains blocked the sunlight, and no lamps were lit. Sheets of paper littered the dim room. Chen Ge picked one up; it showed the same black house crowded with red people.

“Why did you throw these away? Weren’t you satisfied with them?” Holding the drawing, Chen Ge looked toward the table. Fan Yu sat with his back to him, lost in a daze.

Chen Ge picked his way around the papers. One last drawing lay on the table: a house outlined in black crayon, with a tiny black figure standing alone at its center.

“What happened to the red people?”

Chen Ge did not expect an answer, but Fan Yu turned toward him and whispered, “They found a new home.”

“Meaning, they have moved away?” Chen Ge was reminded of the twenty-four uniforms he had seen inside his Haunted House and something clicked. “Are you friends with them?”

The boy shook his head. Without looking away from his drawing, Fan Yu reached into a drawer and handed Chen Ge a cardboard box.

“For me?” Inside lay twenty-four school name tags, each bearing a different name. A group photograph rested in the center, showing twenty-four students with their backs to the camera.

The name tags might unlock the sealed classroom’s mystery, and now Fan Yu had entrusted them to him. Once the box changed hands, the boy fell silent. Chen Ge could not guess his thoughts.

Silence stretched between them. Chen Ge did not have the heart to ask the question on his mind. Then footsteps sounded in the corridor, and a man and woman appeared at the door.

“This should be the place.”

“Why isn’t the door locked? Fan Yu? Are you inside?”

Hearing them, Chen Ge ran out to see what was wrong. “And you are?”

“We’re from the Jiujiang Children’s Home. Here is our identification. We’ve come to take Fan Yu for a medical examination and complete the paperwork for his placement,” the woman explained. Both workers regarded Chen Ge with suspicion, plainly wondering why a strange man was in the boy’s home.

“Fan Yu is inside the bedroom. The boy is very independent, so please do take care of him.”

“We will. It’s our job.” The woman entered the bedroom while the man remained outside, watching Chen Ge. Their distrust was obvious. The moment the woman invaded his space, Fan Yu became agitated. He snatched the drawing from the table and dashed for the door.

“Catch him!” the woman shouted. As Fan Yu rushed past, the man caught his arm. Experienced with distressed children, he quickly pinned both arms in a hold that prevented the boy from scratching him or hurting himself.

Fan Yu fought as if his life depended on it. The sight disturbed Chen Ge, who persuaded the man to release him. Once free, the boy made no second attempt to escape. He only clutched his drawing in silence, as though he understood the futility of running.

As they led Fan Yu away, Chen Ge could contain himself no longer. He hurried after the boy, crouched before him, and asked the question that had troubled him for so long.

“You know heaven is inside the well, and you witnessed everything, so why didn’t you say anything?” Chen Ge had never treated Fan Yu as a normal boy—the house of red people had prevented him from doing that.

Fan Yu considered the question without expression. In the end, he offered no answer. He merely raised his head and gave Chen Ge an innocent smile.

Sweat soaked Chen Ge’s back as he watched the boy leave. It was the first time he had ever seen Fan Yu smile. Clutching the box of twenty-four names and its photograph, he returned to New Century Park.

The police station and Fan Yu’s home had consumed most of the morning. By the time Chen Ge reached New Century Park, it was past 10:30 a.m.

After a night of rain, the sun shone brightly. The park’s crowds lifted Chen Ge’s mood—until he noticed the group massed outside his Haunted House.

At first, he mistook them for customers. Up close, he saw that none were queuing for tickets; instead, they had blocked the entrance against genuine visitors.

What’s happening?Chen Ge walked over and realized that Uncle Xu was also there, negotiating with the unruly crowd.

When they saw Chen Ge approach, they quickly surrounded him.
